summary: PJM files tariff revisions under section 205 on November 16, 2026, in a new docket, ER27-522-000. They define Large Computational Load, set a framework for voltage and frequency ride-through and other operating requirements whose details go in PJM's manuals, and add an annual report on the new transmission services.
ask: Accept the revisions effective January 16, 2027, severing the ride-through requirements from the rest if needed to act quickly.

points.point: PJM files in answer to FERC's preliminary finding that its tariff lacks operating requirements for large loads.
points.quote: that PJM’s Tariff appears to be unjust and unreasonable because it lacks provisions addressing ongoing operational requirements for transmission customers taking transmission service on behalf of large loads.

points.point: The requirements apply to Large Computational Loads, a subset of Large Loads PJM sees as riskier to the grid.
points.quote: defining Large Computational Loads, a subset of Large Loads that may pose heightened operational risks in the PJM Region

points.point: The tariff sets the framework; detailed ride-through and other standards go in PJM's manuals.
points.quote: which establishes the necessary groundwork for more detailed ride-through standards to be promulgated through revisions to PJM’s Manuals

points.point: PJM cites a July 22, 2026 event in which about 3.9 GW of large load dropped off the system.
points.quote: on July 22, 2026, an approximately 3.9 GW large load event caused frequency in the Eastern Interconnection to reach 60.092 Hz

points.point: PJM says it already has about 10 GW of computational load.
points.quote: PJM already has approximately 10 GW of computational load in its footprint

points.point: PJM asks for a January 16, 2027 effective date, earlier than its main large-load filing.
points.quote: effective January 16, 2027, which is 61 days after the date of this filing

points.point: PJM consents to FERC severing the ride-through requirements so they can take effect first.
points.quote: PJM consents to severance of the ride-through requirements from Tariff revisions proposed herein that pertain to other operational requirements

points.point: PJM would post an annual report on demand for and use of the new transmission services, as the co-location order directed.
points.quote: PJM proposes to post on its website a report containing information about the demand for and use of

throughLine.text: Filed under section 205 to answer the E-7 finding that PJM's tariff lacks operating requirements for large loads, and on compliance with the E-2 co-location order's annual reporting directive.
